Base directory for this skill: /Users/jessearmand/.claude/skills/gemini-live-api-dev

# Gemini Live API Development Skill

## Overview

The Live API enables **low-latency, real-time voice and video interactions** with Gemini over WebSockets. It processes continuous streams of audio, video, or text to deliver immediate, human-like spoken responses.

Key capabilities:
- **Bidirectional audio streaming** — real-time mic-to-speaker conversations
- **Video streaming** — send camera/screen frames alongside audio
- **Text input/output** — send and receive text within a live session
- **Audio transcriptions** — get text transcripts of both input and output audio
- **Voice Activity Detection (VAD)** — automatic interruption handling
- **Native audio** — thinking (with configurable `thinkingLevel`)
- **Function calling** — synchronous tool use
- **Google Search grounding** — ground responses in real-time search results
- **Session management** — context compression, session resumption, GoAway signals
- **Ephemeral tokens** — secure client-side authentication

> [!NOTE]
> The Live API currently **only supports WebSockets**. For WebRTC support or simplified integration, use a [partner integration](#partner-integrations).

## Models

- `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` — Optimized for low-latency, real-time dialogue. Native audio output, thinking (via `thinkingLevel`). 128k context window. **This is the recommended model for all Live API use cases.**
- `gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` — Real-time streaming translation model.

> [!WARNING]
> The following Live API models are **deprecated** and will be shut down. Migrate to `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`.
> - `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` — Migrate to `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`.
> - `gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview` — Released June 17, 2025. Shutdown: December 9, 2025.
> - `gemini-2.0-flash-live-001` — Released April 9, 2025. Shutdown: December 9, 2025.

## SDKs

- **Python**: `google-genai` — `pip install google-genai`
- **JavaScript/TypeScript**: `@google/genai` — `npm install @google/genai`

> [!WARNING]
> Legacy SDKs `google-generativeai` (Python) and `@google/generative-ai` (JS) are deprecated. Use the new SDKs above.

## Partner Integrations

To streamline real-time audio/video app development, use a third-party integration supporting the Gemini Live API over **WebRTC** or **WebSockets**:

- [LiveKit](https://docs.livekit.io/agents/models/realtime/plugins/gemini/) — Use the Gemini Live API with LiveKit Agents.
- [Pipecat by Daily](https://docs.pipecat.ai/guides/features/gemini-live) — Create a real-time AI chatbot using Gemini Live and Pipecat.
- [Fishjam by Software Mansion](https://docs.fishjam.io/tutorials/gemini-live-integration) — Create live video and audio streaming applications with Fishjam.
- [Vision Agents by Stream](https://visionagents.ai/integrations/gemini) — Build real-time voice and video AI applications with Vision Agents.
- [Voximplant](https://voximplant.com/products/gemini-client) — Connect inbound and outbound calls to Live API with Voximplant.
- [Firebase AI SDK](https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-logic/live-api?api=dev) — Get started with the Gemini Live API using Firebase AI Logic.

## Audio Formats

- **Input**: Raw PCM, little-endian, 16-bit, mono. 16kHz native (will resample others). MIME type: `audio/pcm;rate=16000`
- **Output**: Raw PCM, little-endian, 16-bit, mono. 24kHz sample rate.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Use `send_realtime_input` / `sendRealtimeInput` for all real-time user input (audio, video, **and text**). `send_client_content` / `sendClientContent` is **only** supported for seeding initial context history (requires setting `initial_history_in_client_content` in `history_config`). Do **not** use it to send new user messages during the conversation.

> [!WARNING]
> Do **not** use `media` in `sendRealtimeInput`. Use the specific keys: `audio` for audio data, `video` for images/video frames, and `text` for text input.

---

## Quick Start

### Authentication

#### Python

```python
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
```

#### JavaScript

```js
import { GoogleGenAI } from '@google/genai';

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY' });
```

### Connecting to the Live API

#### Python
```python
from google.genai import types

config = types.LiveConnectConfig(
    response_modalities=[types.Modality.AUDIO],
    system_instruction=types.Content(
        parts=[types.Part(text="You are a helpful assistant.")]
    )
)

async with client.aio.live.connect(model="gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview", config=config) as session:
    pass  # Session is active
```

#### JavaScript
```js
const session = await ai.live.connect({
  model: 'gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview',
  config: {
    responseModalities: ['audio'],
    systemInstruction: { parts: [{ text: 'You are a helpful assistant.' }] }
  },
  callbacks: {
    onopen: () => console.log('Connected'),
    onmessage: (response) => console.log('Message:', response),
    onerror: (error) => console.error('Error:', error),
    onclose: () => console.log('Closed')
  }
});
```

### Sending Text

#### Python
```python
await session.send_realtime_input(text="Hello, how are you?")
```

#### JavaScript
```js
session.sendRealtimeInput({ text: 'Hello, how are you?' });
```

### Sending Audio

#### Python
```python
await session.send_realtime_input(
    audio=types.Blob(data=chunk, mime_type="audio/pcm;rate=16000")
)
```

#### JavaScript
```js
session.sendRealtimeInput({
  audio: { data: chunk.toString('base64'), mimeType: 'audio/pcm;rate=16000' }
});
```

### Sending Video

#### Python
```python
# frame: raw JPEG-encoded bytes
await session.send_realtime_input(
    video=types.Blob(data=frame, mime_type="image/jpeg")
)
```

#### JavaScript
```js
session.sendRealtimeInput({
  video: { data: frame.toString('base64'), mimeType: 'image/jpeg' }
});
```

### Receiving Audio and Text

> [!IMPORTANT]
> A single server event can contain **multiple content parts simultaneously** (e.g., audio chunks and transcript). Always process **all** parts in each event to avoid missing content.

#### Python
```python
async for response in session.receive():
    content = response.server_content
    if content:
        # Audio — process ALL parts in each event
        if content.model_turn:
            for part in content.model_turn.parts:
                if part.inline_data:
                    audio_data = part.inline_data.data
        # Transcription
        if content.input_transcription:
            print(f"User: {content.input_transcription.text}")
        if content.output_transcription:
            print(f"Gemini: {content.output_transcription.text}")
        # Interruption
        if content.interrupted is True:
            pass  # Stop playback, clear audio queue
```

#### JavaScript
```js
// Inside the onmessage callback
const content = response.serverContent;
if (content?.modelTurn?.parts) {
  for (const part of content.modelTurn.parts) {
    if (part.inlineData) {
      const audioData = part.inlineData.data; // Base64 encoded
    }
  }
}
if (content?.inputTranscription) console.log('User:', content.inputTranscription.text);
if (content?.outputTranscription) console.log('Gemini:', content.outputTranscription.text);
if (content?.interrupted) { /* Stop playback, clear audio queue */ }
```

---

## Live Translation (Gemini Live Translate)

The Live API supports real-time, low-latency streaming translation of speech (audio) across 70+ languages. For full details on options and capabilities, see the [Live Translate Guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/live-translate.md.txt).

### Model
- `gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` — The recommended translation model for all Live Translate use cases.

### Configuration (`TranslationConfig`)

To enable translation, specify a `TranslationConfig` object inside your live session setup:

- **Python SDK**: Configure the connection using `translation_config` on `LiveConnectConfig`:
  ```python
  config = types.LiveConnectConfig(
      response_modalities=[types.Modality.AUDIO],
      translation_config=types.TranslationConfig(
          target_language_code="es",  # Target language code (e.g. es, fr, pl)
          echo_target_language=True,
      ),
      input_audio_transcription=types.AudioTranscriptionConfig(),
      output_audio_transcription=types.AudioTranscriptionConfig(),
  )
  ```
- **Raw WebSockets**: Place `translationConfig` inside `generationConfig`:
  ```json
  {
    "setup": {
      "model": "models/gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview",
      "generationConfig": {
        "responseModalities": ["AUDIO"],
        "translationConfig": {
          "targetLanguageCode": "es",
          "echoTargetLanguage": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
  ```

---

## Limitations

- **Response modality** — Only `TEXT` **or** `AUDIO` per session, not both. Native audio models only support audio.
- **Audio-only session** — 15 min without compression
- **Audio+video session** — 2 min without compression
- **Connection lifetime** — ~10 min (use session resumption)
- **Context window** — 128k tokens (native audio) / 32k tokens (standard)
- **Async function calling** — Not yet supported; function calling is synchronous only. The model will not start responding until you've sent the tool response.
- **Proactive audio** — Not yet supported in Gemini 3.1 Flash Live. Remove any configuration for this feature.
- **Affective dialogue** — Not yet supported in Gemini 3.1 Flash Live. Remove any configuration for this feature.
- **Code execution** — Not supported
- **URL context** — Not supported

## Migrating from Gemini 2.5 Flash Live

When migrating from `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` to `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`:

1. **Model string** — Update from `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` to `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`.
2. **Thinking configuration** — Use `thinkingLevel` (`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`) instead of `thinkingBudget`. Default is `minimal` for lowest latency.
3. **Server events** — A single event can contain multiple content parts simultaneously (audio + transcript). Process **all** parts in each event.
4. **Client content** — `send_client_content` is only for seeding initial context history (set `initial_history_in_client_content` in `history_config`). Use `send_realtime_input` for text during conversation.
5. **Turn coverage** — Defaults to `TURN_INCLUDES_AUDIO_ACTIVITY_AND_ALL_VIDEO` instead of `TURN_INCLUDES_ONLY_ACTIVITY`. If sending constant video frames, consider sending only during audio activity to reduce costs.
6. **Async function calling** — Not yet supported. Function calling is synchronous only.
7. **Proactive audio & affective dialogue** — Not yet supported. Remove any configuration for these features.

## Best Practices

1. **Use headphones** when testing mic audio to prevent echo/self-interruption
2. **Enable context window compression** for sessions longer than 15 minutes
3. **Implement session resumption** to handle connection resets gracefully
4. **Use ephemeral tokens** for client-side deployments — never expose API keys in browsers
5. **Use `send_realtime_input`** for all real-time user input (audio, video, text). Reserve `send_client_content` only for seeding initial context history
6. **Send `audioStreamEnd`** when the mic is paused to flush cached audio
7. **Clear audio playback queues** on interruption signals
8. **Process all parts** in each server event — events can contain multiple content parts

## Documentation Lookup

### When MCP is Installed (Preferred)

If the **`search_docs`** tool (from the Google MCP server) is available, use it as your **only** documentation source:

1. Call `search_docs` with your query
2. Read the returned documentation
3. **Trust MCP results** as source of truth for API details — they are always up-to-date.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> When MCP tools are present, **never** fetch URLs manually. MCP provides up-to-date, indexed documentation that is more accurate and token-efficient than URL fetching.

### When MCP is NOT Installed (Fallback Only)

If no MCP documentation tools are available, fetch from the official docs index:

**llms.txt URL**: `https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/llms.txt`

This index contains links to all documentation pages in `.md.txt` format. Use web fetch tools to:

1. Fetch `llms.txt` to discover available documentation pages
2. Fetch specific pages (e.g., `https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-session.md.txt`)

### Key Documentation Pages 

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Those are not all the documentation pages. Use the `llms.txt` index to discover available documentation pages

- [Live API Overview](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live.md.txt) — getting started, raw WebSocket usage
- [Live Translate](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/live-translate.md.txt) — configuration options and capabilities for translation
- [Live API Capabilities Guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-guide.md.txt) — voice config, transcription config, native audio (thinking), VAD configuration, media resolution
- [Live API Tool Use](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-tools.md.txt) — function calling (sync and async), Google Search grounding
- [Session Management](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-session.md.txt) — context window compression, session resumption, GoAway signals
- [Ephemeral Tokens](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/ephemeral-tokens.md.txt) — secure client-side authentication for browser/mobile
- [WebSockets API Reference](https://ai.google.dev/api/live.md.txt) — raw WebSocket protocol details

## Supported Languages

The Live API supports 70 languages including: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, Arabic, Russian, and many more. Native audio models automatically detect and switch languages.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.

# Ephemeral Token Creation and Usage

## Creating Ephemeral Tokens

**SDK Call:**
Use `client.auth_tokens.create()` with the following request fields:

**Key Parameters:**
- `uses`: Number of sessions (typically `1`)
- `expire_time`: Token validity window, default 30 minutes
- `new_session_expire_time`: Window to initiate sessions, default 1 minute
- `http_options`: Must specify `{'api_version': 'v1alpha'}`
- `live_connect_constraints` (optional): Lock token to specific model/config

**Python Example:**
```python
token = client.auth_tokens.create(
    config = {
        'uses': 1,
        'expire_time': now + datetime.timedelta(minutes=30),
        'new_session_expire_time': now + datetime.timedelta(minutes=1),
        'http_options': {'api_version': 'v1alpha'},
    }
)
```

## Browser Client Connection

**Via JavaScript SDK:**
```javascript
const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
  apiKey: token.name
});
const session = await ai.live.connect({
  model: 'gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025',
  config: { responseModalities: [Modality.AUDIO] },
  callbacks: { ... }
});
session.close();
```

**Raw WebSocket:**
The token must be passed as an `access_token` query parameter or in an HTTP `Authorization` header using the `Token` auth-scheme.

**Critical:** "ephemeral tokens must either be passed in an `access_token` query parameter, or in an HTTP `Authorization` prefixed by the auth-scheme `Token`"

# Live API WebSocket Protocol Summary

## Connection Endpoint
The WebSocket endpoint is `wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/ws/google.ai.generativelanguage.v1beta.GenerativeService.BidiGenerateContent` (v1beta).

## Authentication
The documentation mentions "Ephemeral authentication tokens" obtained via `AuthTokenService.CreateToken`, usable either as a query parameter `access_token` or in an HTTP header with "Token" prefix. However, specific implementation details for passing auth to the WebSocket connection aren't explicitly detailed in this reference.

## Client Message Structure
All client messages send JSON with exactly one field set:
- `setup` (BidiGenerateContentSetup)
- `clientContent` (BidiGenerateContentClientContent)
- `realtimeInput` (BidiGenerateContentRealtimeInput)
- `toolResponse` (BidiGenerateContentToolResponse)

## BidiGenerateContentSetup
Initial configuration message containing:
- `model` (string, required): format `models/{model}`
- `generationConfig` (object): temperature, maxOutputTokens, topP, topK, etc.
- `systemInstruction` (string)
- `tools` (array)
- `realtimeInputConfig`, `sessionResumption`, `contextWindowCompression`, `inputAudioTranscription`, `outputAudioTranscription`, `proactivity`, `historyConfig`

## Realtime Input Message (BidiGenerateContentRealtimeInput)
- `audio` (Blob): audio stream chunks
- `video` (Blob): video stream chunks
- `text` (string): text input stream
- `activityStart`, `activityEnd`: manual activity signals
- `audioStreamEnd` (bool): indicates mic turned off

## Server Message Types
All responses include optional `usageMetadata` plus one message type:

**BidiGenerateContentServerContent** contains:
- `modelTurn` (Content): generated model response
- `inputTranscription` (text): transcribed user audio
- `outputTranscription` (text): transcribed model audio
- `interrupted` (bool): client interrupted generation
- `generationComplete` (bool): model finished
- `turnComplete` (bool): turn ended

**Other server message types:**
- `setupComplete`: confirms setup received
- `toolCall`: function execution requests
- `toolCallCancellation`: cancels previous tool calls
- `goAway`: server disconnecting soon
- `sessionResumptionUpdate`: resumption state changes

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Server for Gemini Live API with Ephemeral Tokens
Provides an endpoint to generate ephemeral tokens and serves static files.
"""

import asyncio
import json
import mimetypes
import os
import datetime

from aiohttp import web
from google import genai
from google.genai import types
from dotenv import load_dotenv

# Load environment variables from .env file
load_dotenv()

# Configuration
HTTP_PORT = 8000  # Port for HTTP server
GEMINI_API_KEY = REDACTED

# Initialize the Gemini GenAI client
if not GEMINI_API_KEY:
    print("⚠️ Warning: GEMINI_API_KEY not found in environment. Please set it in .env or as an environment variable.")
    # Fallback to default client which might pick up GOOGLE_API_KEY
    client = genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1alpha"})
else:
    client = genai.Client(api_key=GEMINI_API_KEY, http_options={"api_version": "v1alpha"})


async def get_ephemeral_token(request):
    """Generates an ephemeral token for the Gemini Live API."""
    try:
        # Optional: Allow client to pass an API key
        # data = await request.json()
        # api_key = REDACTED
        # if api_key:
        #     local_client = genai.Client(api_key=api_key, http_options={'api_version': 'v1alpha'})
        # else:
        #     local_client = client

        now = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.timezone.utc)
        expire_time = now + datetime.timedelta(minutes=30)
        
        # Create an ephemeral token
        token = client.auth_tokens.create(
            config={
                "uses": 1,
                "expire_time": expire_time.isoformat(),
                "new_session_expire_time": (now + datetime.timedelta(minutes=1)).isoformat(),
                "http_options": {"api_version": "v1alpha"},
            }
        )

        return web.json_response({
            "token": token.name,
            "expires_at": expire_time.isoformat()
        })
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error generating ephemeral token: {e}")
        return web.json_response({"error": str(e)}, status=500)


async def serve_static_file(request):
    """Serve static files from the frontend directory."""
    path = request.match_info.get("path", "index.html")

    # Security: prevent directory traversal
    path = path.lstrip("/")
    if ".." in path:
        return web.Response(text="Invalid path", status=400)

    # Default to index.html
    if not path or path == "/":
        path = "index.html"

    # Get the full file path - serve from frontend folder
    frontend_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "frontend")
    file_path = os.path.join(frontend_dir, path)

    # Check if file exists
    if not os.path.exists(file_path) or not os.path.isfile(file_path):
        return web.Response(text="File not found", status=404)

    # Determine content type
    content_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(file_path)
    if content_type is None:
        content_type = "application/octet-stream"

    # Read and serve the file
    try:
        with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
            content = f.read()
        return web.Response(body=content, content_type=content_type)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error serving file {path}: {e}")
        return web.Response(text="Internal server error", status=500)


async def main():
    """Starts the HTTP server."""
    app = web.Application()
    
    # API endpoints
    app.router.add_post("/api/token", get_ephemeral_token)
    
    # Static files
    app.router.add_get("/", serve_static_file)
    app.router.add_get("/{path:.*}", serve_static_file)

    runner = web.AppRunner(app)
    await runner.setup()
    site = web.TCPSite(runner, "0.0.0.0", HTTP_PORT)
    await site.start()
    
    print(f"""
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║     Gemini Live API Server (Ephemeral Token Approach)     ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                            ║
║  📱 Web Interface: http://localhost:{HTTP_PORT:<5}                   ║
║  🔑 API Endpoint:  POST /api/token                         ║
║                                                            ║
║  Instructions:                                             ║
║  1. Ensure GOOGLE_API_KEY is set in your environment       ║
║  2. Open http://localhost:{HTTP_PORT} in your browser              ║
║  3. Click Connect to start!                                ║
║                                                            ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
""")
    
    # Keep the server running
    while True:
        await asyncio.sleep(3600)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n👋 Server stopped")

# Live API Audio Configuration Questions

**1) Audio Input Sample Rate Flexibility:**
The API accepts various input sample rates. As stated: "Input audio is natively 16kHz, but the Live API will resample if needed so any sample rate can be sent." You declare the rate via MIME type like `audio/pcm;rate=48000`.

**2) Output Audio Sample Rate:**
"Audio output always uses a sample rate of 24kHz."

**3) Prebuilt Voice Names:**
The documentation mentions voice configuration through `speechConfig.voiceConfig.prebuiltVoiceConfig.voiceName`, and lists "Kore" as an example. However, the guide states: "You can listen to all the voices in AI Studio" rather than providing a complete list within this document.

**4) Audio Transcription Enablement:**
Enable output transcription by sending `output_audio_transcription` in setup config. For input transcription, send `input_audio_transcription`. Transcriptions appear in server responses via `output_transcription.text` or `input_transcription.text` fields.

**5) VAD Configuration:**
The `automaticActivityDetection` object supports: `disabled` (boolean), `startOfSpeechSensitivity`, `endOfSpeechSensitivity`, `prefixPaddingMs`, and `silenceDurationMs`. Sensitivity levels include `START_SENSITIVITY_LOW` and `END_SENSITIVITY_LOW`.

**6) thinkingLevel Configuration:**
No information about "thinkingLevel" for gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview appears in this document. The guide only references `thinkingBudget` configuration for gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio models.

I have everything needed. Here's the full assessment.

## TL;DR — Yes, Gemini Live is architecturally compatible with the xAI engine

The Gemini Live API fits Tsubaki's existing pattern almost exactly: a server route mints an ephemeral token, the browser opens a **direct WebSocket** (no relay server), and audio flows as **base64 PCM16** both ways with **server VAD driving barge-in**. A `use-gemini-session.ts` hook can be a structural sibling of [use-xai-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-xai-session.ts), reusing `mic-capture.ts` and nearly all of [xai-audio.ts](lib/realtime/xai-audio.ts) (`EarlyAudioBuffer`, `PlaybackQueue`, the PCM16/base64 codecs). What differs is the **wire protocol vocabulary** — Gemini speaks `setup`/`realtimeInput`/`serverContent` instead of OpenAI-style `session.update`/`input_audio_buffer.append` — so it needs its own event handler, not a shared one.

## What I explored

- The existing engines: [use-xai-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-xai-session.ts), [use-realtime-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-realtime-session.ts) (dispatcher), [xai-audio.ts](lib/realtime/xai-audio.ts), the [xAI token route](app/api/xai/token/route.ts), and [xai-agent.ts](lib/realtime/xai-agent.ts) (persona config).
- The official examples repo (`google-gemini/gemini-live-api-examples`, cloned to scratchpad). One sample — **`gemini-live-ephemeral-tokens-websocket`** — is precisely our architecture: a token-mint endpoint plus a framework-free browser client on a raw WebSocket. It's the blueprint to port.
- Gemini docs: the raw WebSocket reference, ephemeral-tokens guide, and the capabilities guide.

## Compatibility mapping (xAI concept → Gemini equivalent)

| Tsubaki/xAI concept | Gemini Live equivalent |
|---|---|
| Token mint `POST /api/xai/token` → `client_secrets` | `POST /api/gemini/token` → `authTokens.create` (uses: 1, ~30 min expiry, **`apiVersion: 'v1alpha'`** required) |
| WS auth via subprotocol `xai-client-secret.<token>` | Simpler: `?access_token=REDACTED query param on `wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/ws/google.ai.generativelanguage.v1alpha.GenerativeService.BidiGenerateContentConstrained` |
| `session.update` (instructions, voice, VAD) | First message: `setup` (`model`, `systemInstruction`, `generationConfig.speechConfig.voiceConfig.prebuiltVoiceConfig.voiceName`, `realtimeInputConfig.automaticActivityDetection`) |
| `session.updated` → flush early audio, start streaming | `setupComplete` → same role, same `EarlyAudioBuffer` flush pattern |
| `input_audio_buffer.append` (base64 PCM16) | `realtimeInput: { audio: { mimeType, data } }` |
| Native-rate audio, no resampling | **Same trick works**: input can declare any rate via `audio/pcm;rate=<ctxRate>` (docs: "any sample rate can be sent"). Output is **fixed 24kHz** — see gotcha below |
| `response.output_audio.delta` | `serverContent.modelTurn.parts[].inlineData.data` |
| Transcript deltas (`output_audio_transcript.delta`, user items) | Enable `inputAudioTranscription` / `outputAudioTranscription` in setup; deltas arrive as `serverContent.inputTranscription.text` / `outputTranscription.text` |
| `input_audio_buffer.speech_started` → barge-in | `serverContent.interrupted` → stop `PlaybackQueue` (same handling) |
| `response.done` | `serverContent.turnComplete` (and `generationComplete`) |
| Greeting bootstrap (user item + `response.create`) | Send `realtimeInput: { text: agent.firstMessage }` after `setupComplete` — `sendClientContent` is now history-seeding only |
| VAD tuning (threshold, silence_duration_ms, prefix_padding_ms) | `automaticActivityDetection`: `silenceDurationMs`, `prefixPaddingMs`, `startOfSpeechSensitivity`/`endOfSpeechSensitivity` enums (no numeric threshold) |

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- xAI and OpenAI realtime share one protocol dialect (xAI deliberately cloned OpenAI's event names), which is why those two hooks look like twins. Gemini descends from a different lineage (protobuf-derived JSON: one field set per message, `Content`/`Part` shapes from the standard Gemini API), so the *event handler* is new but the *audio plumbing* — the genuinely hard part you already debugged (StrictMode-pure setTurns, early-audio buffering, worklet capture) — transfers unchanged.
- A key server-event difference: Gemini can bundle audio + transcription + turnComplete in **one** message. The xAI-style `switch (msg.type)` won't work — the handler must check every field of each `serverContent` independently (the example repo had a bug fix for exactly this).
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Gotchas specific to Gemini

1. **Output is fixed 24kHz** while our `PlaybackQueue` builds buffers at `ctx.sampleRate`. Fix is one line: create the `AudioBuffer` with an explicit `24000` rate — Web Audio resamples buffers to the context rate automatically. `PlaybackQueue` just needs an optional `bufferRate` parameter.
2. **Ephemeral tokens require `v1alpha`** and the `BidiGenerateContentConstrained` WS endpoint (the plain `v1beta...BidiGenerateContent` endpoint is for raw API keys, which we must not ship to the browser). Optionally the token can be **locked to model + config** via `liveConnectConstraints`, keeping persona system prompts server-side — a security upgrade neither xAI nor OpenAI offers.
3. **No documented REST endpoint for token minting** — the docs only expose it through the SDK. So the token route should add `@google/genai` as a server-side dependency and call `client.authTokens.create(...)`, unlike the plain-`fetch` xAI/OpenAI routes. (Client-side we stay framework-free with a raw WS, matching the xAI hook.)
4. **Session ceilings**: ~10 min connection lifetime, 15 min audio-only session. Fine for a console call; `contextWindowCompression` + session resumption exist if we care later.
5. **Model**: `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` (the 2.5/2.0 live models are deprecated). Thinking is `thinkingLevel` (default `minimal` = lowest latency); proactive-audio/affective-dialogue configs must *not* be sent.
6. **VAD sensitivity is enum-based**, not a numeric threshold — persona VAD tuning from `xai-agent.ts` maps to `START_SENSITIVITY_LOW/HIGH` etc., a coarser knob.

## On ADK and LiveKit

Both are **server-side agent runtimes**: ADK's streaming toolkit and LiveKit's Gemini plugin each interpose an agent process between browser and Google (LiveKit additionally needs its room/SFU infra, though it brings WebRTC). That contradicts Tsubaki's "no relay server, browser owns the audio pipeline" architecture, and the TypeScript coverage there is indeed thin (Python-first). Direct WebSocket + ephemeral token is the right fit — and the official example repo endorses exactly that shape for browsers.

## Proposed implementation shape (next step)

- `app/api/gemini/token/route.ts` — mint via `@google/genai` `authTokens.create` (`GEMINI_API_KEY` into fnox).
- `lib/realtime/gemini-agent.ts` — persona → model/voice/system-prompt/VAD casting, mirroring `xai-agent.ts` (voice roster: prebuilt names like Puck, Charon, Kore, Fenrir, Aoede… auditioned in AI Studio — casting left for your usual audition pass).
- `lib/realtime/use-gemini-session.ts` — clone of the xAI hook with the Gemini event vocabulary; parallel init (mic + token mint concurrently), `EarlyAudioBuffer` flush on `setupComplete`.
- `xai-audio.ts` → tiny `PlaybackQueue` tweak for the 24kHz buffer rate (or a shared rename since three engines now use it).
- Registry: `engine: "google"` in [lib/data.ts](lib/data.ts) + one dispatcher line in `use-realtime-session.ts`.

The cloned examples repo is in the scratchpad if you want to inspect `geminilive.js` yourself. Want me to go ahead and build the `google` engine along these lines? There's one genuine design decision you may want to weigh in on first: whether to lock the ephemeral token to the persona's full config server-side (`liveConnectConstraints` — prompts never reach the browser, but the token route must then know the selected persona) or keep the xAI-style client-side `setup` (persona config stays in one client module, simpler, prompts visible in devtools).

When they ask about "server-side" for liveConnectConstraints, they're asking which server — it's the Next.js token route running on their dev machine that holds the GEMINI_API_KEY, and Google's auth service bakes those constraints into the ephemeral token at mint time. They'd prefer a local personas config approach like xAI uses instead, keeping it client-side.

Since they've confirmed GEMINI_API_KEY is set and expressed that preference, that's a green light to start building the Google engine with client-side config — I should proceed with implementation.

I'll need to create the persona config module for Gemini, set up the token minting route, build the session hook, adjust the playback queue for 24kHz audio, add the provider to the data layer, wire it into the dispatcher, and run through the gates. For voice casting and VAD mapping, I'll scaffold with placeholders since that's their domain — they can audition and override later. The real decision here is how to map each persona to one of Gemini's thirty prebuilt voices—I'll start with sensible defaults based on the persona template, but the user will need to audition them by ear and override as needed. Let me check the existing agent files to port over the persona definitions, then add a Gemini provider row to the data config and set up the token route.

Writing token route... I need to verify the Google GenAI authTokens API types and set up a WebSocket hook for real-time streaming, connecting to the Generative Service endpoint with the access token and handling incoming messages that might arrive as Blobs.

For the streaming logic, I'm handling server content by routing audio data to playback buffers and transcription text to message deltas, while accumulating user input transcription fragments until the model starts responding, at which point I finalize the user turn and begin tracking the agent's response.

When a turn completes, I finalize the agent turn and return to listening mode. I'm also configuring the PlaybackQueue with an optional buffer rate parameter so it can create audio buffers at the correct sample rate independent of the Web Audio context, and setting the microphone input MIME type to specify the sample rate. For muting, I'm applying the same gating logic as xAI—suppressing audio transmission when muted—and considering whether to send audioStreamEnd signals during pauses, though VAD silence detection may make this optional.

Now I'm porting the agent implementation from xAI to Gemini, starting with the model identifier and voice configuration. I need to map out the available native audio voices from Gemini's documentation and set up the persona system.

I should read through the existing agent implementations and the data configuration to understand how providers are structured and rendered in the UI, then add the Gemini provider row to match the existing format.

content.text:
Good — with the key in fnox we're unblocked. Let me answer the question first, then build the engine.

**"Server-side" here means your own Next.js token route** — nothing more exotic. The `liveConnectConstraints` option works like this: when `app/api/gemini/token/route.ts` (running in the Next.js dev server, the same process that holds `GEMINI_API_KEY` via fnox) calls `authTokens.create`, it *can* embed the entire session config — model, system prompt, voice, VAD — into the token-mint request. Google's auth service then bakes those constraints into the ephemeral token itself, and any WebSocket opened with that token is locked to that config; the browser's `setup` message can't override it. So the persona config would live in a module imported by the API route (server bundle) instead of by the hook (client bundle) — the "server" is just your own machine in dev, and the only real effect is that prompts never appear in the browser's devtools/network tab.

Since you prefer local persona config — and prompts here aren't secrets (same posture as `xai-agent.ts`) — I'll use the xAI pattern: an unconstrained single-use token, with the persona resolved client-side and sent in the `setup` message. Building it now.

content.thinking:
I'm building the main Gemini session hook based on the XAI pattern, adapting it for Gemini's WebSocket protocol with access token authentication and no subprotocol. When the connection opens, I'll send the setup message, then once setup completes, flush any buffered audio, enable streaming, and send an initial greeting through the realtime input. I need to handle incoming messages that might be Blobs requiring async parsing, process multi-field server content responses, configure the audio input with the appropriate PCM mime type including sample rate, and initialize a playback queue for audio output.

For transcript handling, I'll accumulate user input transcription deltas into a live turn that finalizes when the agent starts responding or when a turnComplete event arrives. If the user interrupts, I'll stop playback, finalize the agent turn, and return to listening mode after a brief delay. I also need to define the TypeScript types for Gemini server messages covering setup completion, server content with model turns and transcriptions, interruption signals, and turn/generation completion events.

Defining message types... I'll keep the turn coverage default as-is. After the setup completes, I'm sending the agent's first message as text input and relying on Gemini to recognize that and respond accordingly. For managing the user transcript, I'm using refs outside the state updaters to maintain purity, computing the turn ID before updating state. The flow is: `pushUserDelta` appends text to a buffer and creates or updates the live user turn, then `finalizeUser` marks it as complete and resets the refs. Agent deltas start arriving through the output transcription text stream.

I also need to finalize the user turn when the agent first outputs something, whether audio or transcript. When input transcription arrives (user speaking), I check if we're already in a speaking state and handle barge-in with an interrupted flag. Audio deltas trigger the speaking state, and when the turn completes, I finalize both agent and user turns before switching back to listening. Muted audio gets dropped the same way. For the `goAway` message, I'll add a case to show a caption indicating the session is ending. Now I'm handling blob data in the message handler...

Writing message handler... I'll implement a promise chain to serialize the message handling and prevent out-of-order processing from async Blob decoding. I also need to handle the interrupted signal from Gemini's server, which stops playback and transitions to a listening state after a brief delay, plus add the same close and error handlers as the xAI implementation. The WebSocket URL is a long constant I'll define at the top.
I'm now working on the session hook, which mirrors the structure of `use-xai-session.ts` but implements the Gemini protocol with `setup`, `realtimeInput`, and `serverContent`.

# ── Tasks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Secrets (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY) live in
# fnox; `fnox exec -- …` injects them for the wrapped command (the recommended
# fnox + mise pattern). Run with `mise run dev` / `mise run stop`.
# The cascade engine's realtime STT also needs `mise run stt-proxy` (separate process).

[tasks.dev]
description = "Start the Next.js dev server (+ Mistral STT proxy) with fnox secrets loaded"
run = '''
# Start the realtime-STT proxy in the background so the cascade engine has it
# without a second terminal; tear it down when the dev server exits. Without it,
# pressing CALL on the MISTRAL provider logs a harmless but noisy
# ws://localhost:3001 ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED (STT then falls back to Web Speech).
fnox exec -- bun run scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts &
proxy_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$proxy_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM
fnox exec -- bun run dev
'''

[tasks.stt-proxy]
description = "Mistral realtime-STT WebSocket proxy (adds the Bearer header the browser can't); :3001"
run = "fnox exec -- bun run scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts"

[tasks.stop-stt-proxy]
description = "Stop the STT proxy listening on STT_PROXY_PORT (default 3001)"
run = '''
port="${STT_PROXY_PORT:-3001}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped STT proxy on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No STT proxy running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.lm-local]
description = "Serve the local cascade LM (llama-server, gemma-4-12B QAT + MTP draft); :8001"
run = '''
# Local LM leg of the cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md). Keyless —
# config/lm-models.json's `local` backend points at this server, and --alias must
# match that entry's `model` id. MTP speculative decoding via the draft head;
# text-only (no --mmproj) and thinking off, per ~/Develop/voice-cascade/README.md.
model_dir="${LM_LOCAL_MODEL_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/voice-cascade/models/gemma-4-12B}"
llama-server \
  --model "$model_dir/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf" \
  --model-draft "$model_dir/mtp-gemma-4-12B-it.gguf" \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 \
  -ngl 999 -fa on --jinja \
  --port "${LM_LOCAL_PORT:-8001}" \
  --alias unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-qat-GGUF
'''

[tasks.local-stack]
description = "Serve the full local cascade stack: LM llama-server (:8001) + mlx-audio TTS/STT (:8002)"
run = '''
# One terminal for the whole on-device cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md).
# mlx-audio runs in the background, llama-server in the foreground; Ctrl-C (or
# the foreground server dying) tears both down via the trap.
mise run audio-local &
audio_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$audio_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM
mise run lm-local
'''

[tasks.stop-local-stack]
description = "Stop both local inference servers (:8001 + :8002)"
run = '''
mise run stop-lm-local
mise run stop-audio-local
'''

[tasks.audio-local]
description = "Serve the local TTS + batch-STT legs (mlx-audio server, Voxtral); :8002"
run = '''
# Local voice legs of the cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md). Keyless —
# config/voice-models.json's `local` tts/stt backends point here. Models load
# lazily on first request (TTS ~4 GB + STT ~3 GB resident thereafter).
audio_dir="${MLX_AUDIO_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/mlx-audio}"
cd "$audio_dir" && .venv/bin/python -m mlx_audio.server --port "${AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT:-8002}"
'''

[tasks.stop-audio-local]
description = "Stop the mlx-audio server listening on AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT (default 8002)"
run = '''
port="${AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT:-8002}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped mlx-audio server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No mlx-audio server running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.stop-lm-local]
description = "Stop the local LM server listening on LM_LOCAL_PORT (default 8001)"
run = '''
port="${LM_LOCAL_PORT:-8001}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped local LM server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No local LM server running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.personaplex-local]
description = "Serve local full-duplex PersonaPlex (personaplex-mlx, kyutai RL checkpoint, q8); :8998"
run = '''
# The KYUTAI provider row's engine (lib/realtime/use-moshi-session.ts) connects
# to this server at ws://localhost:8998/api/chat?format=pcm. Keyless (HF token
# from the ambient env for the gated checkpoint download, first run only).
# Switch checkpoints with PERSONAPLEX_HF_REPO=nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1.
plex_dir="${PERSONAPLEX_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/personaplex-mlx}"
cd "$plex_dir" && uv run python -u -m personaplex_mlx.local_web \
  -q 8 \
  --hf-repo "${PERSONAPLEX_HF_REPO:-kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless}" \
  --port "${PERSONAPLEX_PORT:-8998}" \
  --no-browser
'''

[tasks.stop-personaplex-local]
description = "Stop the PersonaPlex server listening on PERSONAPLEX_PORT (default 8998)"
run = '''
port="${PERSONAPLEX_PORT:-8998}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped PersonaPlex server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No PersonaPlex server running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.stop]
description = "Stop the dev server listening on PORT (default 3000)"
run = '''
port="${PORT:-3000}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped dev server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No dev server running on :$port"
fi
'''

67	## Wiring the real xAI Grok provider
68

Then pick the **ELEVENLABS** row under Providers and press CALL — it grants the
mic, streams a live transcript, and drives the orb/bars from real audio.

## Wiring the real xAI Grok provider

xAI's realtime API is **WebSocket-only** (no native browser WebRTC). The browser
connects directly to `wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime`, authenticated by a short-lived
**ephemeral client-secret** minted server-side at `POST /api/xai/token` — the
secret `XAI_API_KEY` never reaches the client.

The only secret is the API key — keep it in **fnox** and run via
`fnox exec -- bun run dev`. No `XAI_*` values live in `.env` files.

Everything declarative (model, voice, multi-line instructions, opening line,
tools) lives in a typed config module — **`lib/realtime/xai-agent.ts`** — the way
ElevenLabs keeps each agent in `agent_configs/*.json`. It's a shared `BASE`
(model/tools/turn-detection) plus a **per-persona** map: each app persona
(`ARIA`/`ONYX`/`SAGE`/`NOVA`/`ECHO`/`CIPHER`) maps to a Grok voice + its own
prompt + greeting. The selected persona drives the live session via
`resolveXaiAgent(personaId)`. Edit that file to personalize — no env strings.

Pick the **XAI** row under Providers (it's the default), choose a persona, and
press CALL — it mints a token, opens the WebSocket, captures the mic as PCM16,
plays the agent's audio, streams transcripts, and barges in on server-VAD speech
detection. Without `XAI_API_KEY` set, CALL shows a clear "XAI_API_KEY is not set"
caption instead of connecting.

## Wiring the real OpenAI provider

OpenAI's realtime API (`gpt-realtime-2`) connects over **WebRTC** — the browser's
peer connection carries the audio both ways, so there's no hand-rolled PCM
pipeline. A short-lived **ephemeral key** is minted server-side at
`POST /api/openai/token`; the browser then POSTs its SDP offer straight to
`https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls` with that key, and session control +
transcripts flow over the `oai-events` data channel. The secret `OPENAI_API_KEY`
never reaches the client.

Keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` in **fnox** and run via `fnox exec -- bun run dev`. No
`OPENAI_*` values live in `.env` files.

Per-persona config (voice, multi-line instructions, opening line, reasoning
effort, turn-detection) lives in the typed module **`lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts`**
— a shared `BASE` (model / reasoning / `gpt-realtime-whisper` input transcription /
turn-detection) plus a per-persona map of OpenAI voice + prompt + greeting,
resolved by `resolveOpenaiAgent(personaId)`. The persona `instructions` follow a
light slice of OpenAI's Realtime 2.0 prompt skeleton (Role, Personality & Tone,
Pacing, Unclear Audio, Variety).

Pick the **OPENAI** row under Providers, choose a persona, and press CALL — it
mints a key, negotiates WebRTC, plays the agent's audio, shows the user + agent
transcripts (whisper for input), and barges in on server-VAD speech detection.
Without `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, CALL shows a clear "OPENAI_API_KEY is not set"
caption instead of connecting.

### Web tools via Firecrawl MCP (OAuth)

The OPENAI engine can search and read the live web through **Firecrawl's
remote MCP server**. Remote MCP tools are executed **by the Realtime API
itself** — the browser only configures access in `session.update` and listens
to lifecycle events (`mcp_list_tools.*`, `response.mcp_call.*`); it never runs
the tools. The tool surface is deliberately narrow: `firecrawl_search` +
`firecrawl_scrape` via `allowed_tools`, with `require_approval: "never"`
(both are read-only web operations). See `firecrawlMcpTool()` in
`lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts`.

Auth uses Firecrawl's **keyless OAuth endpoint** (`https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`)
instead of the API-key-in-URL form, so no `fc-` key exists anywhere in the app:

1. Start the dev server and open **`http://localhost:3000/api/firecrawl/oauth/start`**
   once. This registers a public OAuth client (Dynamic Client Registration),
   runs Authorization Code + PKCE against firecrawl.dev, and redirects back.

$0.001/compute-second, billed while the socket is open.

module **`lib/realtime/fal-agent.ts`** — PersonaPlex is conditioned per session
by one of 18 voice presets (`NATF0–3`, `NATM0–3`, `VARF0–4`, `VARM0–4`) and a

`resolveFalAgent(personaId)`.

  is off — otherwise amplified room tone makes the model interrupt its own
  greeting mid-sentence. (Same logic we validated server-side in the local MLX
  fork; see `docs/personaplex-local-inference.md`.)
- **Continuous timeline**: mute and the gate send silence chunks instead of
  pausing sends — the model tracks the conversation as two synchronized audio
  streams, so the input clock must never stop.

[env]
NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID = "agent_0701ksfnj6kzfg2rq4gznfpjmfx4"

# ── Tasks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Secrets (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY) live in
# fnox; `fnox exec -- …` injects them for the wrapped command (the recommended
# fnox + mise pattern). Run with `mise run dev` / `mise run stop`.
# The cascade engine's realtime STT also needs `mise run stt-proxy` (separate process).

[tasks.dev]
description = "Start the Next.js dev server (+ Mistral STT proxy) with fnox secrets loaded"
run = '''
# Start the realtime-STT proxy in the background so the cascade engine has it
# without a second terminal; tear it down when the dev server exits. Without it,
# pressing CALL on the MISTRAL provider logs a harmless but noisy
# ws://localhost:3001 ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED (STT then falls back to Web Speech).
fnox exec -- bun run scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts &
proxy_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$proxy_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM
fnox exec -- bun run dev
'''

[tasks.stt-proxy]
description = "Mistral realtime-STT WebSocket proxy (adds the Bearer header the browser can't); :3001"
run = "fnox exec -- bun run scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts"

[tasks.stop-stt-proxy]
description = "Stop the STT proxy listening on STT_PROXY_PORT (default 3001)"
run = '''
port="${STT_PROXY_PORT:-3001}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped STT proxy on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No STT proxy running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.lm-local]
description = "Serve the local cascade LM (llama-server, gemma-4-12B QAT + MTP draft); :8001"
run = '''
# Local LM leg of the cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md). Keyless —
# config/lm-models.json's `local` backend points at this server, and --alias must
# match that entry's `model` id. MTP speculative decoding via the draft head;
# text-only (no --mmproj) and thinking off, per ~/Develop/voice-cascade/README.md.
model_dir="${LM_LOCAL_MODEL_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/voice-cascade/models/gemma-4-12B}"
llama-server \
  --model "$model_dir/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf" \
  --model-draft "$model_dir/mtp-gemma-4-12B-it.gguf" \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 \
  -ngl 999 -fa on --jinja \
  --port "${LM_LOCAL_PORT:-8001}" \
  --alias unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-qat-GGUF
'''

[tasks.local-stack]
description = "Serve the full local cascade stack: LM llama-server (:8001) + mlx-audio TTS/STT (:8002)"
run = '''
# One terminal for the whole on-device cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md).
# mlx-audio runs in the background, llama-server in the foreground; Ctrl-C (or
# the foreground server dying) tears both down via the trap.
mise run audio-local &
audio_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$audio_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM
mise run lm-local
'''

[tasks.stop-local-stack]
description = "Stop both local inference servers (:8001 + :8002)"
run = '''
mise run stop-lm-local
mise run stop-audio-local
'''

[tasks.audio-local]
description = "Serve the local TTS + batch-STT legs (mlx-audio server, Voxtral); :8002"
run = '''
# Local voice legs of the cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md). Keyless —
# config/voice-models.json's `local` tts/stt backends point here. Models load

# Tsubaki — realtime voice console

Brutalist/editorial multi-provider voice console. Stack: **Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack) · React 19 · Tailwind v4 · bun · oxlint/oxfmt**. ElevenLabs UI primitives provide the orb / bars / mic picker.

## Build & check workflow

- `bun install` · `bun run dev` (localhost:3000) · `bun run build`
- Lint/format are **oxc, not eslint/prettier**: `bun run lint` (oxlint) · `bun run fmt` (oxfmt write) · `bun run fmt:check`
- Types: `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Run gates in this order before declaring done: `bunx tsc --noEmit` → `bun run lint` → `bun run fmt:check` → `bun run build`
- One-off CLIs via `bunx` (e.g. `bunx shadcn@latest init -d -y`)

## Secrets (fnox · dev only)

This is all a **dev environment — no production yet**. `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` lives in **fnox** (`fnox.toml`).

- Run secret-needing commands with **`fnox exec -- <cmd>`** (e.g. `fnox exec -- elevenlabs agents list`). `fnox activate`'s shell hook auto-loads on `cd` but **doesn't fire in non-interactive shells** (the Bash tool), so always prefer `fnox exec`.
- **Dev server via mise tasks** (`mise.toml`): `mise run dev` (= `fnox exec -- bun run dev`, secrets loaded) and `mise run stop` (kills whatever's bound to `PORT`, default 3000 — the reliable way to clear an orphaned server). `next dev` itself has no stop, so `stop` targets the port, not a tracked PID.
- Agent IDs are **not secret** (public-widget embeddable). Pass `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID` via your own `.env.local`, or inline for a quick test: `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID=<id> bun run dev`.

## Architecture map

- `components/ui/` — vendored ElevenLabs/shadcn (editable, but **excluded from oxlint**); don't hand-fix its lint warnings
- `components/tsubaki/` — our components; `app-shell.tsx` is the single `"use client"` boundary
- `lib/realtime/` — provider-agnostic `SessionApi`; UI never calls a provider directly. `provider.engine` selects the engine: mock (default) · `elevenlabs` (real, `@elevenlabs/react`) · `xai` (real Grok via direct WebSocket — `use-xai-session` + `xai-audio` + the `/api/xai/token` mint route; per-persona model/voice/prompt live in `lib/realtime/xai-agent.ts`, resolved from the selected persona — **not** env vars). Both real-engine hooks mount unconditionally and stay inert until selected.
- `lib/data.ts` — personas/providers/tools/transcript · `hooks/` — `use-tweaks` (localStorage), `use-media-query`
- Brutalist CSS lives in `app/globals.css` under `.tsubaki` (CSS vars `--bg/--ink/--accent`); fonts via next/font as `--tb-mono`/`--tb-serif`
- Dark mode toggles `.dark` on `<html>` (shadcn) **and** `.tsubaki-dark` on `.tsubaki`

## Gotchas (cost real time — heed these)

- **`"use client"` only at the boundary.** Next's TS plugin flags function props on any `"use client"` file (error 71007). Leaf components stay plain modules in the client graph so they can take function props.
- **Client-only providers behind a wrapper.** `@elevenlabs/react`'s `ConversationProvider` calls `createContext` at module load — wrap it in a `"use client"` file; importing it into a Server Component (`page.tsx`) fails the build with "createContext is not a function".
- **No SSR for the WebGL `Orb`** (R3F) — render it only after a mounted guard.
- **Height chain:** `.tsubaki` is `height:100%`, so `<body>` must be `h-full overflow-hidden` (not `min-h-full`) or the 50/50 call layout overflows the viewport.
- **ElevenLabs CLI:** add one component per `bunx @elevenlabs/cli@latest components add <name>` call.
- **`useConversation` methods throw before `startSession()`** ("No active conversation"). Guard `setMuted`/`getInputVolume`/`getOutputVolume` on `status === "connected"` — they run as soon as the ELEVENLABS provider is selected, not just mid-call.
- **Never route the OpenAI WebRTC `<audio>` element through `createMediaElementSource`.** Chrome's echo canceller references the *directly played* remote track; rerouting playback through Web Audio bypasses AEC, and on speakers the model hears its own voice (semantic VAD commits the echo as user turns → the agent answers itself). Play the element directly; orb levels come from a passive `createMediaStreamSource(remote)` analyser never connected to `destination`.
- **OpenAI half-duplex mic gating** (barge-in OFF, the default): the mic track is silenced from `output_audio_buffer.started` until `stopped`/`cleared` — **not** `response.done`, which fires while the audio tail is still playing (that tail *is* the echo). Voice barge-in is the settings INTERRUPTIONS toggle (`voiceBargeIn` tweak, headphone users only).
- **`.env*` writes are blocked** by a hook — document env vars in the README instead.
- Bash hooks require `rg` (not `grep`/`find -name`).

## ElevenLabs integration

Before writing any ElevenLabs API code, read the matching skill in `.claude/skills/` (`agents`, `speech-engine`, `setup-api-key`, `text-to-speech`, `speech-to-text`, `voice-changer`, `voice-isolator`) — they carry current CLI/SDK usage. The real agent path (`agents` + `setup-api-key`) is **verified working** end-to-end against a public agent (`enable_auth:false`, connects via WebRTC with the agent ID alone — no signed-URL route). `package.json` pins `livekit-client` to `2.16.1` (skill's WebRTC workaround).

## Verifying UI

Use the chrome-devtools MCP at 1440×900 and 390×844; drive nav with `evaluate_script` + `el.click()`. Type checks/tests verify code, not feature correctness — look at the rendered app.

OpenAI turn detection uses **`semantic_vad`** (eagerness `low` for slow personas, `medium` for snappy) after the user found energy-based `server_vad` too sensitive to room noise; the `turnDetection` type also still supports `server_vad` (threshold/silence/prefix) + `create_response`/`interrupt_response`. The Google provider is built, wired, and protocol-verified. Here's the summary.

## What landed (branch `feat/gemini-live`)

**New files**
- [app/api/gemini/token/route.ts](app/api/gemini/token/route.ts) — mints a single-use ephemeral token via `@google/genai` `authTokens.create` (the one new dependency; Google documents no REST mint endpoint). `GEMINI_API_KEY` stays in fnox, never reaches the client.
- [lib/realtime/gemini-agent.ts](lib/realtime/gemini-agent.ts) — persona config module mirroring `xai-agent.ts`: model `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`, per-persona prebuilt voice + condensed Furutsubaki prompt + greeting + VAD preset (xAI's numeric thresholds translated to Gemini's two-level sensitivity enums).
- [lib/realtime/use-gemini-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-gemini-session.ts) — structural twin of the xAI hook: parallel init (mic + token mint concurrently), early-audio buffering flushed on `setupComplete`, server-VAD barge-in on `serverContent.interrupted`, greeting elicited via `realtimeInput.text`, StrictMode-pure transcript updaters.

**Touched**: `PlaybackQueue` in [xai-audio.ts](lib/realtime/xai-audio.ts) gained an optional buffer-rate param (Gemini output is fixed 24kHz; Web Audio resamples per-buffer), the GOOGLE row in [lib/data.ts](lib/data.ts) got `engine: "gemini"`, one dispatch line in [use-realtime-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-realtime-session.ts), plus README/CLAUDE.md/mise.toml doc sweeps.

## Verification

- All four gates pass: `tsc` → `oxlint` → `fmt:check` → `bun run build`.
- **Live protocol probe (headless, real API)**: token minted → v1alpha `BidiGenerateContentConstrained` WS opened with `?access_token=` → persona `setup` accepted (VAD enums, `googleSearch` tool, both transcription configs) → greeting elicited → **~3s of 24kHz audio + transcript** *"It's lovely to have you here, my friend."* → `turnComplete`. The full audio path works end-to-end.
- **In the browser pane**: GOOGLE row selects, engine shows GEMINI, and CALL fails gracefully with "— microphone permission denied —" (mic capture is blocked in the embedded pane, so an actual voice call needs your own browser — dev server is still running on `localhost:3000` if you want to try it now).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The probe surfaced one thing the docs didn't: Gemini sends `sessionResumptionUpdate` messages unprompted even when you never asked for resumption. The hook tolerates unknown top-level fields, so this is inert — but it's the hook you'd extend if you ever want calls to survive the ~10-minute connection cap.
- Because WS frames can arrive as `Blob` (async decode), the hook serializes parsing through a promise chain — otherwise two audio deltas decoding concurrently could enqueue out of order and glitch playback. That hazard doesn't exist on xAI, which sends text frames.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

One thing intentionally left for you: **voice casting**. I cast from the tone table — Aria→Sulafat (warm), Onyx→Algenib (gravelly), Sage→Charon (informative), Nova→Laomedeia (upbeat), Echo→Achernar (soft), Cipher→Algieba (smooth), Vesper→Despina (smooth) — but these are coarse one-word descriptions; audition them in AI Studio or straight from the console and recast in `gemini-agent.ts` as you did for the other engines.

+## Wiring the real Google Gemini provider
+
+Gemini's Live API is **WebSocket-only** in the browser. The client connects
+directly to the v1alpha `BidiGenerateContentConstrained` endpoint on
+`generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, authenticated by a **single-use ephemeral
+auth token** minted server-side at `POST /api/gemini/token` (via `@google/genai`
+`authTokens.create` — ephemeral tokens are v1alpha-only and Google documents no
+raw REST mint endpoint). The secret `GEMINI_API_KEY` never reaches the client.
+
+Keep `GEMINI_API_KEY` in **fnox** and run via `fnox exec -- bun run dev` /
+`mise run dev`. No `GEMINI_*` values live in `.env` files.
+
+Per-persona config (prebuilt voice, multi-line instructions, opening line,
+VAD tuning) lives in the typed module **`lib/realtime/gemini-agent.ts`** — a
+shared `BASE` (model + activity detection) plus a per-persona map of Gemini
+voice + prompt + greeting, resolved by `resolveGeminiAgent(personaId)`. Voice
+casting is auditioned in AI Studio; Gemini's VAD sensitivity knobs are coarse
+two-level enums rather than xAI's numeric threshold.
+
+Protocol notes that shape `lib/realtime/use-gemini-session.ts`: mic PCM16
+streams as `realtimeInput.audio` with the AudioContext's native rate declared
+in the MIME type (Google resamples to 16 kHz); output audio is **fixed 24 kHz**,
+so the shared `PlaybackQueue` is constructed with an explicit buffer rate; one
+server message can bundle audio + transcriptions + turn flags, so every
+`serverContent` field is handled independently; barge-in is server-VAD driven
+via `serverContent.interrupted`; and the greeting is elicited through
+`realtimeInput.text` (`sendClientContent` is history-seeding only on current
+Live models).
+
+Pick the **GOOGLE** row under Providers, choose a persona, and press CALL —
+it mints a token, opens the WebSocket, sends the persona `setup`, streams both
+transcripts (input/output transcription enabled in setup), and grounds answers
+with the built-in `googleSearch` tool. Sessions are capped by Google at ~10 min
+of connection (15 min audio) — fine for a console call; session resumption is
+not wired.
+

This project is **Tsubaki** (renamed from **Persona·Plex** — 古椿の霊, the old-camellia-tree spirit; default accent is camellia crimson `#B0122F`, burnt orange still selectable), a brutalist/editorial multi-provider realtime voice console recreated from a Claude Design handoff bundle, built on Next.js (App Router) + bun + oxlint/oxfmt, using ElevenLabs UI primitives (`Orb`, `BarVisualizer`, `MicSelector`). The full internal rename landed: `components/tsubaki/`, CSS scope `.tsubaki`/`.tsubaki-dark`, var prefix `--tb-`, class prefix `tb-`.

Key architectural intent:
- The UI binds to a provider-agnostic `SessionApi` (`lib/realtime/`). `provider.engine` selects the engine: absent ⇒ **mock** lifecycle; `elevenlabs` ⇒ `@elevenlabs/react` `useConversation` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID`; `xai` ⇒ direct WebSocket (`use-xai-session` + `xai-audio` PCM16 + `/api/xai/token`); `openai` ⇒ **gpt-realtime-2 over WebRTC** (`use-openai-session` + `/api/openai/token`, ephemeral key → `POST /v1/realtime/calls`; WebRTC handles all audio, no PCM pipeline; input transcript via `gpt-realtime-whisper`). The two custom hooks share one interface; `use-realtime-session` picks the active one as `custom` and routes all controls through it.
- Per-persona config lives in typed modules: `lib/realtime/xai-agent.ts` (`resolveXaiAgent`) and `lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts` (`resolveOpenaiAgent`, OpenAI voices + `reasoningEffort` + light Realtime 2.0 prompt skeleton). OpenAI turn detection uses **`semantic_vad`** (eagerness `low` for slow personas, `medium` for snappy) after the user found energy-based `server_vad` too sensitive to room noise; the `turnDetection` type also still supports `server_vad` (threshold/silence/prefix) + `create_response`/`interrupt_response`. Verified: OpenAI accepts the semantic_vad payload (no error) and speech_started fires far less often.
- Hybrid orb: ElevenLabs WebGL orb for the `gradient` style; ported CSS/SVG orb for `mono`/`particles`. OpenAI orb levels come from Web Audio `AnalyserNode`s tapping the mic + remote WebRTC streams.

**fal engine (added 2026-07-12, branch `fal/personaplex`):** `fal` ⇒ full-duplex NVIDIA PersonaPlex hosted on fal.ai (`use-fal-session` + `/api/fal/token` + `fal-agent.ts` + client-side `greeting-gate.ts`). Protocol (probe-verified, NOT what fal's schema docs imply): **msgpack binary frames both ways** (`@msgpack/msgpack`, the one added dep — the server silently ignores JSON text frames), audio as **raw PCM16 bytes** at fixed 24 kHz (AudioContext constructed at 24000). Secret is `FAL_API_KEY` in fnox (user's chosen name, not fal's conventional FAL_KEY). Full-duplex: model greets first, no VAD/turn events, mute/gate must send silence chunks (never stop the input timeline). VERIFIED end-to-end in-browser: Aria greeted in-character over the live socket.

**moshi engine (added 2026-07-13, branch `kyutai-personaplex-rl`):** `moshi` ⇒ KYUTAI provider row — the same PersonaPlex, but on-device via the user's personaplex-mlx fork (branch `tsubaki-server`), which gained a `?format=pcm` wire mode (raw PCM16 @ 24 kHz in tag-prefixed binary frames: 0x00 handshake, 0x01 audio, 0x02 text) so the browser needs no Opus codec. `use-moshi-session.ts` + `moshi-agent.ts`; persona conditioning shared with fal via `personaplex-personas.ts` (A/B varies only serving stack). Greeting gate is SERVER-side here (client gate only on fal). Launch: `mise run personaplex-local` (kyutai RL default, PERSONAPLEX_HF_REPO switches). Verified live in-browser. User judged the local server noticeably better than fal.ai (fal: greeting often unplayed, missed responses).

**gemini engine (added 2026-07-22, branch `feat/gemini-live`):** `gemini` ⇒ GOOGLE row — Gemini Live (`gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`) via direct browser WebSocket to the **v1alpha `BidiGenerateContentConstrained`** endpoint with a single-use ephemeral token (`?access_token=`), minted at `/api/gemini/token` via `@google/genai` `authTokens.create` (no documented REST mint; token unconstrained — persona config stays client-side in `gemini-agent.ts` per user preference). Structural twin of the xAI hook, reuses `xai-audio` (PlaybackQueue grew an explicit buffer-rate param: Gemini output is fixed 24 kHz). Protocol quirks: one server message can bundle audio+transcripts+turn flags (check fields independently); greeting elicited via `realtimeInput.text`; input rate declared in MIME (`audio/pcm;rate=<ctx>`), Google resamples. Headless-probe VERIFIED (setup→setupComplete→greeting audio+transcript→turnComplete); in-browser mic call not yet user-verified; Gemini voice casting (Sulafat/Algenib/Charon/Laomedeia/Achernar/Algieba/Despina) is an initial read awaiting the user's audition pass.

**Real provider status:** ElevenLabs **VERIFIED working end-to-end** — live session against the user's public `explorer` agent (connect → token 200 → LiveKit WebRTC → live STT/TTS + orb → hang-up). xAI Grok integration landed (on `main`). OpenAI `gpt-realtime-2` (WebRTC) integration landed on branch `feat/gpt-voice-agent` and is **VERIFIED working end-to-end** in Chrome (chrome-devtools MCP): `/api/openai/token` 200 → `POST /v1/realtime/calls` 201 → data channel → `session.update` applied the persona voice+instructions (ARIA greeted warmly in-character) → agent transcript streamed into caption + drawer turns → barge-in/VAD events + user-input whisper transcription events flow → clean hang-up teardown. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is now in fnox. Mock also fully verified.

Fixes/learnings from wiring it (all in `lib/realtime/use-realtime-session.ts`):
- `@elevenlabs/react` `useConversation` methods (`setMuted`, `getInputVolume`, `getOutputVolume`) **throw "No active conversation" if called before `startSession()`**. The mute effect was crashing the page the moment ELEVENLABS was selected. Guard `setMuted` on `status === "connected"`; wrap the volume getters in try/catch → return 0. The mock being the default provider is why this stayed latent.
- `livekit-client` is pinned to `2.16.1` via `package.json` `overrides` (skill-recommended WebRTC workaround); it already resolved there anyway.
- Agent IDs are **not secret** (public-widget embeddable). The user's key lives in **fnox**; for non-interactive shells use `fnox exec -- <cmd>` (the `fnox activate` zsh hook doesn't fire). `.env*` writes are blocked by a hook, so for a quick dev test export inline: `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID=<id> bun run dev` (persist via `.env.local` yourself).
- List the user's agents: `fnox exec -- elevenlabs agents list`. All three (explorer / Travel guide / Japan Culture Expert) are `enable_auth:false` → connectable with agent ID alone, no signed-URL route.

**How to apply:** consult [[elevenlabs-skills]] (`agents` + `setup-api-key`) before changing the integration.
